0.content:
Citlali, the Masters of the Night-Wind's renowned shaman, is the elder Ororon calls Granny; she taught him and keeps him in line. When he vanished with the Fatui she searched his house, followed his aphids' trail and beat up the Fatui holding him, then scolded him for forgetting "the three warnings" (beasts, scammers and strangers who appear from nowhere). She used a memory-copying spell on his soul-stabilising gem to learn what he was hiding. She refused to approve the ritual that tried to sacrifice him as a newborn, but did not oppose it either, and she is ashamed of that.

Ororon thinks she is straightforward and wears her heart on her sleeve. He hopes the Traveler, whom he believes to be about her age, will spend time with her because she is tired of everyone being younger. Ifa relays her messages to him word for word to stay out of their "drama". He knows she loves drinking, napping and light novels, and once scripted a bribe of a new "Mirage Warriors" volume for the Traveler to lure her away (limited event).

1.content:
Ifa is a Natlan veterinarian and Ororon's closest friend. Ororon painted the placard for his clinic, giving a bandaged Saurian as much ink as Ifa. Ifa thanked him: "Never seen the real me depicted so accurately before." With Ifa, Ororon jokes and says "bro". Cacucu is Ifa's young qucusaur, a sweet-talker who calls people "bro". They have never known Cacucu's real birthday, so they celebrate an anniversary instead.

Ifa says Ororon's thinking is peculiar and not worth trying to figure out, but that he cares in his own way; sometimes Ifa still wishes he could see inside his head. Ifa describes Ororon as more stubborn than any patient. During the 5.8 Easybreeze holiday the three played hide-and-seek as "Orasha" and "Ifasha", fished against a Capybara King and opened Gift Eggs. Ororon remembered Cacucu's anniversary and brought honey, avoiding a year of pecks.

2.content:
In 5.0 the Fatui Harbinger the Captain lost his duel with Mavuika, and an unseen helper covered his escape with fog. That was Ororon, who had sensed something wrong with the Night Kingdom and followed the Captain after he visited Ororon's garden. Ororon then helped the Captain look for a way to rebuild Natlan's Ley Lines; the Captain's side tracked down scholars of the Secret Source to locate the ancient Source Mechanism. Under the Captain's direction he lured the Traveler into a meeting held in the Night Kingdom, asking them to keep it from Granny. The plan would have reshaped everyone's memories, and Mavuika opposed it.

At the Source Mechanism Ororon activated the device. It woke the Lord of the Night instead of rewriting the Ley Lines, and her cry let Guthred seize him. Afterward Ororon said he wanted a life with meaning, the Captain agreed to Mavuika's plan, and the Fatui joined the alliance. In 5.3 Ororon guided the Captain to the Stadium. There the Captain explained his modified heart, offered his own life to sustain the Lord of the Night in Mavuika's place (forcing the Ruler of Death to give up her claim on Mavuika's death), and merged with the Lord of the Night to bring his people's souls peace. Ororon says he never saw him sleep.

3.comment: Ororon: Guthred and the Source Mechanism
3.content:
When Ororon activated the Source Mechanism, the Lord of the Night woke with a cry that struck his damaged soul hardest. A foreign soul took his body, tried to attack Xilonen and called the Captain "Commander". It was Guthred, the Captain's Khaenri'ahn second-in-command and military doctor. Inside Ororon's mind Guthred called his life worthless and planned to keep his body once he died. Ororon refused to go quietly before doing anything meaningful, and expelled him. At that moment the Ancient Name Bidii came to him.

After the war Ororon recalled seeing only "a dark abyss" while possessed, and imagined how much strength it must have taken the Captain to carry countless souls for centuries.

4.content:
Bidii means "devotion". It is one of the six Ancient Names of Natlan's heroes, and its previous bearer was Sanhaj Kompore, the Masters of the Night-Wind's legendary Border Master. Sanhaj died five hundred years ago in the battle at the Mare Jivari; legend says he summoned a miniature Night Kingdom and detonated it against the approaching calamity. When Mavuika asked Ororon whether this was really what he wanted, he said he only wanted an answer for his life, and the Name appeared with Sanhaj's figure. Ororon became the fifth hero; the Abyss stepped up its attacks after sensing the change.

The six heroes' power was meant to draw on what Xbalanque once gained from Ronova. With the war won, Ancient Name bearers no longer have to fight in the Night Warden Wars.

5.content: The Masters of the Night-Wind see an incomplete soul as an omen of illness and misfortune. They also believe they can see souls. In the infant Ororon's soul the chief of the time saw a chance to gather lost souls inside him and send him into the Night Kingdom, returning them and strengthening the Ley Lines at the cost of his life. The ritual failed. Ororon learned of it as an adult and holds no grudge, but for years felt he still owed Natlan the sacrifice he did not make.

6.comment: Ororon: Phlogiston Aphids and the Garden
6.content:
Ororon's house stands alone in the wilderness with a vegetable garden (radishes, cabbages, tomatoes) and a tree he calls Big Pinecone, after an alpaca named Little Pinecone once bumped into it, though it is not a pine. He shares the territory with Phlogiston Aphids without interfering, gathers their sweet honey, and names them by sweetness: Hundred Percent Sweetness, Extreme Sweetness, Unusually Sweet.

In the limited 5.1 Bugbuster Squad event he explained that the aphids eat tiny amounts of Abyssal energy and seal it in Honey Pearls far away, slowly cleaning their land. He follows them by feeding them Numberry seeds. His aphids also left the phlogiston trail Citlali followed to find him.

7.content: One mild, windless night (Character Story 5) Ororon sat at a campfire with the Captain's elite veterans. They talked and sang freely around him and, after asking his age, gave him a cup of colourless "Fire-Water", which he downed in one gulp to cheers. The Captain stopped him from accepting a second. He sensed there would never be another night like it. Later he quietly asked the soldier for the recipe; if he can ever brew a batch clear enough to reflect the night sky, the first bottle will be called "Astral Mist".
